title: Layers of the Theodosian Walls
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Place the five layers of Constantinople's land walls on a schematic cross-section in the order an attacker from the west met them, then answer three questions on why the design worked.

learningObjectives: Identify the five layers of the Theodosian land walls in the order an attacker from the west meets them, with no more than one placement error.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Retrieval practice: label a diagram, then explain
keyQuestions: What does an army from the west meet first, and what last?
Why is the inner wall taller than the outer wall?
Which emperor completed the land walls in 413?
How did the crusaders get into the city in 1204?
commonMisconceptions: The walls were one thick wall.
The moat was the strongest defense.
The outer wall was taller than the inner wall.
The walls were named for Theodosius I.
The land walls were breached before 1453 (the crusaders entered from the harbor in 1204).
assessmentOpportunities: First-submission score on the five positions (mastery: 4 of 5).
Score on the three Part 2 questions.
Explain why a breach in the outer wall still left the defenders a chance.
